fix.notes: Pure CSS change to a single file. The negative-margin technique mirrors how other full-bleed elements (e.g. .card-information-warning) already work in this codebase. The mobile media query breakpoint (900px) matches the existing override for main/header/footer padding.
fix.pr_body:
## What was wrong

The notice (banner) element that advertises events like the PD500 was constrained by `main`'s horizontal padding (`--spacing-page-with-marginalia`). The background color was applied to `.notice p` rather than `.notice` itself, so there was no way for it to visually break out of the content margins.

## What changed

In `shared_web/static/css/pd.css`:
- Added a `.notice` rule that moves `background: var(--tertiary-background)` from `.notice p` to `.notice`, and applies negative horizontal margins equal to `--spacing-page-with-marginalia` so the banner bleeds to the viewport edge.
- Updated `.notice p` to use `padding: 1em var(--spacing-page-with-marginalia)` so text stays visually indented to the page margin.
- Added a `@media (max-width: 900px)` block that mirrors the existing mobile override for `main` and `header`, resetting the margins to `-1rem` and padding to `1rem` on small screens.

No HTML changes were required.

## Validation

`uv run --frozen python dev.py lint` — passed. This is a CSS-only change with no Python logic; no unit tests cover CSS layout.

Fixes #12218
fix.pr_title: Stretch notice banner to full browser width (#12218)

evidence.detail: main has 'padding: 0 var(--spacing-page-with-marginalia)' which constrains all children including .notice
.notice p carries background: var(--tertiary-background) but .notice has no negative margins, so the colored background stops at main's padding edge — exactly the reported problem
--spacing-page-with-marginalia: calc(96rem / 20) is available as a CSS var for the negative-margin calc
.notice div is directly inside <main>, which is the padded container

Add a @media (max-width: 900px) override using -1rem. No HTML changes needed.
